title: Infant septic shock (meningococcal)
stem: Paediatric resus. An 8-month-old boy has had a fever since this morning and is now floppy with a spreading rash. HR 195, BP 62/30, RR 52, SpO2 94% in air, temperature 39.4 °C, capillary refill 5 seconds. His mother is with him. The paediatric team is 10 minutes away.

phases.title: ABCDE
phases.goal: Monitoring and his weight; assess him A to E, including the rash and a glucose.

phases.title: Resuscitate
phases.goal: Oxygen, access, cultures, ceftriaxone within the hour, 10 mL/kg, glucose; no LP now.

phases.title: Reassess
phases.goal: After each bolus; fluid-refractory at 40 mL/kg: adrenaline infusion.

phases.title: Talk and call
phases.goal: His mother, PICU and an anaesthetist, public health.

events.say: Reassessed: HR 185, CRT 4 seconds. Still shocked.
40 mL/kg in: still HR 180, CRT 4 seconds, cool to the knees.

review.text: Fluid bolus size. Your WETFLAGS and sepsis notes use 20 mL/kg. RCUK/ERC (2021 onwards) and NICE use 10 mL/kg, reassessing after each bolus; after 40–60 mL/kg start inotropes and involve PICU.
Antibiotic. Your notes give cefuroxime 50 mg/kg. For meningococcal sepsis, NICE uses ceftriaxone 80 mg/kg IV within 1 hour (cefotaxime in neonates; add amoxicillin under 3 months).
Bolus size. AHA PALS allows 10–20 mL/kg boluses; RCUK/NICE use 10 mL/kg. The script uses 10 mL/kg and reassesses after each, which every scheme accepts.

notes:
Checked against RCUK 2025 paediatric life support, NICE NG51 (Suspected sepsis, updated 2024), NICE CG102 (Bacterial meningitis and meningococcal disease in under 16s), and the Surviving Sepsis Campaign paediatric guidelines (2020).

Weight: APLS (age in months ÷ 2) + 4 = 8 kg.

Fluid: 10 mL/kg boluses of balanced crystalloid (or 0.9% saline) over 5–10 minutes, reassessing after each for response and overload (crackles, hepatomegaly, rising work of breathing); after 40–60 mL/kg, start inotropes (adrenaline, which can run peripherally or IO at low concentration) and involve PICU. Your notes' WETFLAGS and sepsis sections use 20 mL/kg boluses; RCUK/ERC 2021 onwards and NICE use 10 mL/kg, so 20 mL/kg is not scored.

Access: IV, and IO if IV fails in 90 seconds (or immediately in shock).

Antibiotics within 1 hour: ceftriaxone 80 mg/kg IV (NICE; cefotaxime in neonates or with calcium infusions; add amoxicillin under 3 months). Your notes list cefuroxime 50 mg/kg; that is not first-line for meningococcal sepsis.

Glucose: correct hypoglycaemia with 10% glucose 2 mL/kg (as in your notes). Check calcium. Notify public health; prophylaxis for close contacts.

Perfect script checked against an RCUK/NICE paediatric sepsis checklist, an AHA PALS septic shock checklist, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Added: weight said aloud, the diagnosis named, no LP stated with its reason, reassessment for overload, glucose rechecked, an anaesthetist for intubation, contact prophylaxis. The circulation check now plays the pulse close-up (it played the glucose meter).

script.say: Monitoring on, please: ECG, blood pressure and SpO2. He's 8 months old: about 8 kg. High-flow oxygen, 15 litres via a non-rebreather.

Airway patent; RR 52 with mild recession, chest clear. Heart rate 195, capillary refill 5 seconds centrally, weak pulses, BP 62/30, mottled: decompensated shock. Liver 1 cm below the costal margin: a baseline before fluids.
He responds to pain only, the fontanelle is full and he's floppy. He has a non-blanching purpuric rash: it stays under the glass. This is meningococcal septic shock. Glucose, please.

IV access; if it isn't in within 90 seconds, IO in the proximal tibia. Blood cultures, a gas with glucose and calcium, FBC, CRP, clotting, U&E and meningococcal PCR, without delaying the antibiotic. No lumbar puncture now: he's shocked with a full fontanelle.
Ceftriaxone 80 mg per kg, 640 mg, IV or IO, within the first hour. A fluid bolus of 10 mL per kg, 80 mL, over 5 to 10 minutes. And 2 mL per kg of 10% glucose for the hypoglycaemia.
Reassess after each bolus: heart rate, capillary refill, the liver edge and the chest for overload. Recheck his glucose after the dextrose.
Still shocked: a second and third 10 mL per kg bolus, checking for fluid overload each time.
script.do: After 40 mL per kg: still HR 180, CRT 4 seconds, cool to the knees.

script.say: Fluid-refractory at 40 mL per kg: an adrenaline infusion, 0.05 to 0.1 micrograms per kg per minute, which can run peripherally or IO.
He's very unwell with a serious blood infection. We're giving antibiotics and fluids now, and the intensive care team is coming. You can stay with him.

PICU and retrieval: an 8 kg infant with meningococcal septic shock, fluid-refractory after 40 mL per kg, adrenaline running, glucose corrected. He'll need intubation: please bring an anaesthetist. Notify public health: his close contacts and family need antibiotic prophylaxis.
